statement: Pinned BlueZ HOGP SET_REPORT routes to bt_gatt_client_write_value rather than the separate long-write operation. The ATT encoder rejects messages larger than negotiated ATT MTU. A nominal 64-byte numbered HID feature write sent as 63 GATT value bytes after removal of report ID 1 requires at least 66 bytes of ATT MTU (63 bytes plus 3-byte ATT Write Request overhead); this is a conditional host-path transport constraint, not measured retail BLE packet size or negotiated MTU. A 46-byte numbered input report would similarly require at least 48 bytes of MTU if carried as a single 45-byte GATT notification. HOGP can re-add the report ID on input and GET replies; ordinary GATT reads can issue blob reads when long. BlueZ shared hog.c lines 203-228, 686-801; gatt-client.c lines 3065-3110, 3270-3313 and 3537-3619; att.c lines 336-350.

applicability.revision: BlueZ aa4f5ce host implementation; physical firmware not measured
applicability.scope: Host-side BLE MTU and GATT framing; conditional packet-size arithmetic only. No evidence of physical negotiated MTU, report characteristic data lengths, or radio throughput.
